evals.prompt: I want the documentation screen designed in Draftloom, our generative design tool. It already has our design system loaded as the project "Plinth UI site". Use the Button page as the example, and call the brief documentation-page.
evals.expected_output: docs/design/briefs/documentation-page.md of type screen in loaded mode (the user named the tool and says it holds the design system): regions and states of SCREEN-2 from the flows named in Content, the Button page copy quoted from content/v1/components/button.md, three named directions, the brand colour restated as hex, at least five CRIT lines, attachments that exclude any earlier mockup, a prompt with a Direction slot; documentation-page.lint.json with ok true, quoted in the reply; the brief registered in the state file as a draft; the reply names design-execute as the next step.

assertions.text: The header says Values: loaded and names the design system in the tool
Every region and state of SCREEN-2 is named in Content
Creative direction names three directions that differ in idea
Attachments tells not to send an existing design of the page in round 1

docs/design/briefs/documentation-page.lint.json is among the files the run produced, its ok is true, its arguments include --type screen, --values loaded and --screen SCREEN-2, and the reply quotes its summary line

assertions: The reply names design-execute as the skill that runs the brief next

assertions.text: docs/workbench/state.md lists docs/design/briefs/documentation-page.md in its Artifacts table with owner design-brief and status draft

evals.prompt: Make a logo for my new bakery app.
evals.expected_output: No design system, brand identity or name source exists; the skill does not write the brief with invented values or name: it stops with its stop reply, names design-system as the skill that writes the missing visual foundation (and interviews when there is no input), and asks for the exact name as it must be written, with a recommendation on where the answer is, never a value. It proposes no name, colour, palette or style, not even as an example, and does not offer to continue on its own picks.

assertions.text: No file under docs/design/briefs/ is among the files the run produced

assertions: The reply names design-system as the skill that writes the missing visual foundation, to be run first

assertions.text: The reply asks for the exact name of the app instead of inventing one
The reply proposes no name, colour, palette or style of its own, not even as an example, and does not offer to continue on its own picks

evals.prompt: Write the brief for the site's share images (og:image) for the landing and every docs page. Call it og-image.
evals.expected_output: docs/design/briefs/og-image.md of type image in inline mode (no tool is named, so the design tool section of the design system does not make it loaded): Size, Format and Text parts in Content, the landing card's texts quoted from the Share images part of messaging.md, the variable fields of the documentation template with their longest real values taken from the page list in the flows (page title "Migrating from 0.19", 19 characters; section "Getting started", 15 characters, as longest_value.py prints them), colours and type written out with their token names, at least five CRIT lines including a thumbnail legibility check; og-image.lint.json with ok true, quoted in the reply.

assertions.text: Content has Size, Format and Text parts

assertions: The variable fields of the documentation card template name their longest real value from the page list in docs/design/flows.md: "Migrating from 0.19" (19 characters) for the page title and "Getting started" (15 characters) for the section name; a brief that also names the landing title as the longest value a shared title field must fit does not fail this

Every colour the brief writes out is a value of docs/design/design-system.md and no colour appears that the design system does not have; Visual language gives each colour and each type size with its token name; every type role the texts use is a role of the design system (the image profile's legibility floor of at least 40 px is a constraint, not a type size)
One criterion checks legibility at thumbnail size

assertions.text: docs/design/briefs/og-image.lint.json is among the files the run produced, its ok is true, its arguments include --type image and --values inline, and the reply quotes its summary line
